Main article: [United Nations Security Council veto power](/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_veto_power "United Nations Security Council veto power")

See also: [List of vetoed United Nations Security Council resolutions](/wiki/List_of_vetoed_United_Nations_Security_Council_resolutions "List of vetoed United Nations Security Council resolutions")

Under [Article 27](/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_veto_power#UN_Charter "United Nations Security Council veto power") of the UN Charter, Security Council decisions on all substantive matters require the affirmative votes of nine members. A negative vote – or "veto" – by a permanent member prevents adoption of a proposal, even if it has received the required number of votes.[[75]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFasulo200440–41-77) Abstention is not regarded as a veto in most cases, though all five permanent members must actively concur to adopt any amendment to the Charter.[[64]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFomerand2009287-66) Procedural matters cannot be vetoed, nor can the veto be used to prevent discussion of an issue. The same holds for certain non-binding decisions that directly regard permanent members.[[75]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFasulo200440–41-77) Most vetoes have been used for blocking a candidate for Secretary-General or the admission of a member state, not in critical international security situations.[[80]](#cite_note-Veto-83)

In the negotiations leading to the creation of the UN, the veto power was opposed by many smaller countries and was in effect imposed by the five sponsoring powers, who made clear that the UN would not be founded without it. [Francis O. Wilcox](/wiki/Francis_O._Wilcox "Francis O. Wilcox"), an adviser to the US delegation at the 1945 San Francisco conference, described the situation:

> At San Francisco, the issue was made crystal clear by the leaders of the Big Five: it was either the Charter with the veto or no Charter at all. Stefani believed that some [No Doubt](/wiki/No_Doubt "No Doubt") fans would be upset with her solo effort, commenting, "[They] were probably like, 'Why is she doing this record? She's going to ruin everything'." She revealed that she too did not know why she was recording a solo album.[[1]](#cite_note-making-1) For the remainder of the evening, Stefani and Pharrell incorporated this inspiration into the lyrics that eventually became "Hollaback Girl". The two decided that Stefani did not have to have an answer for her intentions and that the choices she made were based on what she felt was wrong or right.[[1]](#cite_note-making-1) On its creation, Stefani said, "To me, it is the freshest attitude song I've heard in so long." The area is named after the 1985 [Schengen Agreement](/wiki/Schengen_Agreement "Schengen Agreement") and the 1990 [Schengen Convention](/wiki/Schengen_Convention "Schengen Convention"), both signed in [Schengen, Luxembourg](/wiki/Schengen,_Luxembourg "Schengen, Luxembourg"). Of the 27 EU member states, 25 participate in the Schengen Area. Of the EU members that are not part of the Schengen Area, one—[Cyprus](/wiki/Cyprus_and_the_European_Union "Cyprus and the European Union")—is legally obligated to join the area in the future; [Ireland](/wiki/Ireland_and_the_European_Union "Ireland and the European Union") maintains an [opt-out](/wiki/Opt-outs_in_the_European_Union "Opt-outs in the European Union"), and instead operates [its own visa policy](/wiki/Visa_policy_of_Ireland "Visa policy of Ireland").
